newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche-Moody's move won't raise refinance cost.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche-Moody's move won't raise refinance cost.

text.p: Germany's Deutsche Bank AG said a decision by Moody's to cut its long term deposit rating to AA1 from AAA would not raise its refinancing costs in the long term.
"Deutsche Bank is convinced that the new rating will not lead to a lasting rise in refinancing costs," the bank said in a statement.
Deutsche also said it would stick to its strategy of combating rising competition through tough cost management and a globally oriented expansion.
Deutsche also said that Moody's rating confirmed Deutsche's credit-standing and said it was among "the strongest financial groups in the world."
The bank added that it remained the only German commercial bank with AAA ratings from Standard & Poor's and IBCA.

In the past, Deutsche chairman Hilmar Kopper has said he would fight any moves by Moody's to strip Deutsche of the highly prized AAA rating, although he also said that any change would not adversely affect Deutsche's international standing.

Deutsche's shares earlier slipped on the Moody's news, which was released minutes ahead of the close of late electronic stock dealings. Deutsche ended down 56 pfennigs at 70.59 marks, while the broader market was slightly firmer.
